newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Telkom sees equity partner by March 1997.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Telkom sees equity partner by March 1997.

text.p: South African telecommunications utility Telkom said on Wednesday the process of selecting a foreign equity partner was on track and would be finalised by the end of March next year.

"The second phase of the due diligence investigation is complete. The process (of finalising an equity partner) is due to be completed by March next year. It is well on track," Telkom managing director Brian Clark told reporters.
The sale of a stake in Telkom to foreign bidders is the first major step in the South African government's privatisation programme and is seen as a litmus test of its commitment to economic reform.
Government last month invited Deutsche Telkom, France Telecom, Telekom Malaysia and South Western Bell (SBC) of the United States to submit detailed bids for a 20 to 30 percent stake in Telkom.
Telkom Malaysia and SBC announced soon after that they would bid as a consortium and Deutsche Telkom and France Telecom said they were considering a joint bid.

Clark was speaking at a presentation to announce local and international call tariff increases and the re-pricing of long distance and local calls in a bid to compete successfully in the global telecommunications market.
"The overall increase for the basket of tariffs for 1997 is seven percent -- two percent below the expected rate of inflation," Clark said, adding that increases would take effect from January 14.
He said the effect of the price increases would be to raise Telkom's income by about seven percent, equivalent to some 790 million rand.
Clark said Telkom's tradition of subsidising local call tariffs by charging higher rates on long distance and international calls would be phased out from the beginning of next year.

An announcement would be made by March 1997 on when Telkom's period of exclusivity, under which it has enjoyed monopoly status, would run out, Clark said. During this time Telkom would reorganise itself to compete globally.
"We aim to use the period of exclusivity to emerge as a balanced, internationally competitive, world class telecommunications company," Clark said.
